public_rationale: The available records describe different things. Cast AI reports low execution utilization in sampled clusters, while Microsoft reports demand above available Azure capacity. Paid capacity can be inefficiently used while providers still face shortages. Neither source settles the ordinary market-demand reading of this claim. Treating 'endless' literally would make the statement uninformative rather than establish the alleged demand problem.
limitations: The practical reading adds a measurable interpretation to rhetorical wording.
The utilization sample is not representative of all AI compute.
Provider capacity statements are self-reported and broader than AI alone.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is not endless, insatiable demand for AI compute.

statement.excerpt: Well, other than the fact there isn’t.

our_interpretation: Read this as a practical claim that demand is insufficient to absorb the AI compute capacity being supplied, not the trivial observation that demand cannot literally be infinite.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed reporting quarter before the post, for the ongoing state.
Distinguish unsold capacity caused by weak demand from idle execution time on capacity customers have already purchased.
The wording supplies no utilization threshold or duration. Do not invent one or require every processor to run continuously.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, representative evidence shows persistent excess AI compute capacity attributable to insufficient demand, supported by utilization, availability, cancellations or comparable rental-price evidence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that demand absorbs available AI compute capacity across the relevant market, with persistent shortages or waiting lists and no material demand-related surplus.

evidence.locator: Section 'The AI Era Is Adding a New Layer of Waste'
evidence.explanation: This documents a disclosure of substantial underutilization in sampled clusters, not unsold market capacity. The date is the disclosure date; the passage does not establish when the GPU measurements were taken.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood, Intelligent Cloud results discussion
evidence.explanation: Microsoft describes shortages during its quarter-end results discussion. This weighs against a broad weak-demand reading, but Azure includes CPU services and the statement is not an independent AI-market utilization measure.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative target-quarter measurements of unsold and contracted AI capacity, utilization and comparable prices, with evidence identifying whether persistent spare capacity resulted from insufficient demand.
